thread:
samir: Hey folks — we just got a support escalation from Acme about higher latencies. p95 for /v1/generate in us-west2 jumped from ~180ms -> 1.2s over the last 30m, p99 at 2.7s. Customer sees timeouts and some 504s. Any quick mitigation playbook we can run?

monitoring-bot: [ALERT] 1727129800 - prod.us-west2/api/p95 > 1s for 5m (metric: request_latency_ms). Affected service: inference-gateway. Tags: model=redwood-7b, tier=hosted

jordan: First cut: enable circuit breaker for the org and route traffic to fallback model. Recommend CB trip at 1200ms, cooldown 10s. Also lower per-org qps to 0.8x (or 50 req/s if org has high quota).

elaine: Agreed. Immediate steps I can run now: 1) throttle org `acme-corp` via console -> org rate limits; 2) flip route to `redwood-3b` in us-west2 fallback; 3) enable reject-on-timeout so callers get 503 instead of hanging.

samir: Jordan, can you paste the exact commands to toggle fallback? I'll perform throttle and restart shards after.

jordan: Sure — use oncall creds.
```
# set route fallback
redwoodctl routing update --selector region=us-west2 --fallback-model redwood-3b
# add circuit breaker
redwoodctl runtime cb set --service inference-gateway --threshold-ms 1200 --cooldown-s 10
# throttle org
redwoodctl orgs rate-limit set acme-corp --rps 50
```

elaine: If we need immediate capacity: scale inferencer pool up (add 2x GPU nodes) or enable burst. Example: 
```
kubectl scale deployment/inferencer-pool -n inference --replicas=8 --selector=region=us-west2
```

samir: I'll lower the org rps and push fallback. Doing throttle now... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

opsbot: action: rate-limit updated for org=acme-corp -> 50 rps by samir

samir: fallback route updated, cb set, scaling up the pool now. Monitor looks better so far.

monitoring-bot: [RECOVERY] 1727132200 - prod.us-west2/api/p95 back to 220ms after throttling + fallback. p99 at 480ms. No errors observed in last 5m.

elaine: Great. Follow-ups (assign):
- file support ticket to Acme summarizing mitigation steps and ask for traffic pattern and recent rollout changes.
- add permanent route fallback + CB to our runbook for sudden p95 spikes for model=redwood-7b.
- consider auto-policy: if p95 > 800ms for >3m then auto-route to smaller model or failover region.

jordan: Also recommend adding a temporary SLO guardrail in the console: event-driven circuit-breaker + token-bucket per org so one noisy tenant can't spike p99 for others. We should capture the rule in policy repo.

samir: Creating a runbook PR now and pinging @oncall_rotation to handoff. Thanks everyone :heart:

oncall_rotation: acknowledged, taking over monitoring for next hour.
